title: Value of White-Box Testing
concept:
White-box (structure-based) testing has value distinct from black-box testing.

**Coverage of code paths the spec doesn't mention** — code often contains paths handling internal states, error recovery, defensive checks, or legacy logic that the spec is silent about. Black-box tests miss these; white-box exposes them.

**Detection of dead code** — code that no input ever reaches is dead code. Coverage tools highlight statements never executed; investigation reveals whether they should be exercised by a missing test or whether they should be deleted.

**Confidence in coverage-based metrics** — when a test plan declares 'we will achieve 90% branch coverage', a coverage tool can verify the claim. This is impossible with black-box techniques alone.

**Driving test case quality** — chasing higher coverage forces the team to think about edge cases, error paths, and combinations that black-box techniques may not surface.

**Limitations** — white-box does not catch missing functionality: a function that simply doesn't exist has zero statements and therefore contributes nothing to coverage. Missing functionality is caught by black-box and requirements-based techniques. The two are complementary, never substitutes.
keyPoints: White-box catches defects in code that black-box wouldn't reveal: undocumented paths, dead code, error-handling branches.
It enables objective coverage metrics that the test plan can target.
It does NOT catch missing functionality — combine with black-box for complete coverage.

quiz.question: Which of the following is a defect that white-box testing is MORE likely to catch than black-box testing?
options: A missing requirement: the spec forgot to mention a feature.
Dead code: a block that no input ever reaches.
A slow response time under heavy load.
quiz.explanation: Dead code is invisible to black-box testing — by definition no input reaches it, so external behaviour is unchanged. White-box coverage tools highlight statements never executed, exposing dead code. Missing requirements, UI usability, and load performance are detected by other methods (review, usability testing, performance testing).
